title: The circumbinary disc of HD 34700A: II. Analysis of a strong dust asymmetry
question: Characterise the crescent morphology of the circumbinary disc around HD 34700A and compare it with IRS 48 and HD 142527, discuss their possible origin, and assess the efficiency of dust trapping in the vortex scenario.

data.bands: Band 6 (1.3 mm) for HD 34700A; Band 7 (0.87 mm) for IRS 48 and HD 142527
data.sensitivity: HD 34700A: 7 uJy beam^-1; IRS 48: 16 uJy beam^-1; HD 142527: 252 uJy beam^-1

what.value: 13CO discminer geometrical fit (inclination and PA) for HD 34700A used as narrow priors

evidence.quote: For the inclination and PA of HD 34700 A, we consider narrow priors around the values resulting from the $^{13}$CO `discminer` (cite: Izquierdo_2021) fit in (cite: Stadler_2026) to help achieve convergence, and be consistent with their analysis.

what.value: Inclination and PA for IRS 48 used as narrow priors

evidence.quote: We use the same procedure for IRS 48, using the inclination and PA reported in (cite: Yang2023).

what.value: Inclination and PA for HD 142527 used for prior setup

evidence.quote: For HD 142527, instead, we setup wider priors around the inclination and PA reported in (cite: vdM2021).

we compute the optical depth $\tau=\sum_i \Sigma_i\kappa_{\mathrm{abs},i}$, with $\Sigma_i$ and $\kappa_{\mathrm{abs},i}$ the surface density and “DSHARP"-mixture absorption opacity associated with grains of size $i$, taken from (cite: Birnstiel_2018)

recipe.goal: Remove secondary companion HD 34700B from visibility table
recipe.method: Create a CLEAN model of HD 34700B within an elliptic mask and subtract model visibilities using CASA uvsub()
key_parameters: CLEAN threshold = 5 uJy/beam (~1 sigma), elliptic mask R = 0.625'', i = 41.5

recipe.goal: Image continuum emission and measure RMS noise, peak intensity, and azimuthal contrast
recipe.method: CLEAN continuum visibilities with CASA tclean, compute RMS in outer annulus and deproject to polar coordinates with gofish, and compute azimuthal contrast
key_parameters: CLEAN threshold = 3 sigma, robust = 0.0 (or 0.5 for IRS 48 in Table 1), pixel sizes 0.015'', 0.009'', 0.025''
Polar interpolation grid: 501 x 2001 (R, theta) with R in [0, 4]'' and theta in [-180, 180] deg
assumptions: 10% ALMA flux calibration uncertainty for Band 6 and 7

recipe.goal: Parametric visibility modelling of circular and eccentric disc morphologies
recipe.method: Fit 2D parametric brightness models (central/offset Gaussian + Gaussian ring + 1 or 2 asymmetric Gaussian arcs) to visibilities using galario and emcee
key_parameters: 15 parameters for HD 34700A, 13 for IRS 48, 23 for HD 142527 (plus eccentricity e and argument of periastron omega for eccentric models)
Preliminary run: 100 walkers, ~10^3 steps; Fiducial run: 120 walkers, 2x10^4 steps, 25% burn-in
assumptions: Inner Gaussian fixed to image centre for HD 34700A; no inner Gaussian for IRS 48; same eccentricity for all ring and arc components in eccentric fits

recipe.goal: Analytical dust trapping modelling of the azimuthal intensity profile
recipe.method: Compute steady-state dust size distribution and azimuthal drift-mixing equilibrium following Birnstiel et al. (2011, 2013), calculate optical depth and intensity, and manually tune parameters to match observed azimuthal profile at 137 au
key_parameters: A_gas = 1.1, sigma_y = 75 deg, alpha = 5x10^-4, Sigma_c = 50 g cm^-2 at R_c = 1 au, v_frag = 5 m s^-1, epsilon = 0.1
assumptions: Vertically isothermal disc with T_dust = T_c(R/R_c)^-0.5, T_c = 20 K at R_c = 100 au; DSHARP dust absorption opacities; steady-state dust size distribution

recipe.goal: Hydrodynamical simulation of dust distribution around a massive vortex and synthetic continuum imaging
recipe.method: Run 2D cylindrical gas+6-dust-fluid hydrodynamical simulation of a Rossby-wave-unstable cavity edge in PLUTO for 100 orbits, compute 230 GHz intensity map, convolve with ALMA beam and add Gaussian noise
key_parameters: R_0 = 150 au, grid 0.4-2.5 R_0, N_R x N_phi = 512 x 1024, M_star = 4 M_sun, alpha = 10^-4, 6 dust sizes a_d = {10^-4, 0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1} cm, rho_bulk = 2.08 g cm^-3, integrated for 100 orbits at R_0
assumptions: Single central star M_star = 4 M_sun, locally isothermal EOS, h = 0.15(R/R_0)^1/4, Sigma_g = 1 g cm^-2 (R/R_0)^-1, Sigma_d = 0.01 Sigma_g, MRN initial grain size slope q = -3.5, Epstein drag

score_reason: The imaging parameters, parametric visibility model equations, priors, MCMC setup, analytical dust trapping parameters, and PLUTO hydrodynamic setup are all thoroughly documented, and all three ALMA project codes are public. However, self-calibration is inherited from external papers, visibility averaging prior to galario fitting is not specified, and minor unit/table inconsistencies exist.
rediscovery_reason: All three ALMA datasets are publicly available in the archive, the continuum imaging and galario visibility modelling recipe is well-specified using standard open-source tools (CASA, gofish, galario, emcee), and the main morphological parameters and contrasts are crisp numeric benchmarks.
